mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 300d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt OM654 engines range from £3,200 to £5,500 depending on engine code and condition. With specialist fitting, budget £3,600-£6,300 total. OM654.920 (E 300d, 245 hp, 2018-2021): rebuilt £3,200-£5,000. OM654.930 (E 300d, 265 hp with EQ Boost, 2021-2023): rebuilt £3,500-£5,500. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in an E Class 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold-start rattle is the classic early warning sign. A recall was issued for OM654 engines in E-Class (213 platform) vehicles due to timing chain bolt and link wear. Rattle on cold start that disappears after a few seconds. Metallic noises from the rear of the engine. Loss of power or engine management light. Timing chain replacement at a specialist costs £1,500-£2,200.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an E Class 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound. W213 E Class 300d examples with good service history still command £18,000-£30,000 used, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt OM654 costs £3,200-£5,500 supply only. The 300d is the most powerful four-cylinder diesel in the E-Class range. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than the depreciation on a newer car. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800, not dealer rates of £1,500+.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM654 timing chain to fail on E Class 300d models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654 timing chain is mounted at the rear of the engine. Individual bolts or chain links can wear under specific driving conditions, leading to a recall for certain vehicles. Chain wear typically occurs between 80,000-120,000 miles. Extended oil change intervals (over 10,000 miles) accelerate wear. Stop-start operation can exaggerate wear. Cold-start rattle is the early warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM654.920 and OM654.930 engines in the E Class 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesels. The OM654.930 (2021-2023) features EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology with 48V starter-generator, producing 265 hp (up from 245 hp) and 550 Nm (up from 500 Nm). OM654.920 fitted to E 300d (2018-2021): 180 kW (245 hp), 500 Nm. OM654.930 fitted to E 300d facelift (2021-2023): 195 kW (265 hp), 550 Nm. Both share the same 82mm bore × 92.3mm stroke. Both suffer from the same timing chain wear concerns.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 300d engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and 8,000-10,000 mile oil changes, OM654 engines regularly reach 200,000-300,000 miles. OM654 is a modern, efficient diesel with robust bottom end. Timing chain inspection/replacement at 80k-100k miles is recommended. Regular AdBlue system maintenance prevents costly tank replacement. Short oil change intervals (8k miles) are critical for timing chain life.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 300d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 300d badge was reintroduced with the W213 E-Class generation in 2018, positioned as the most powerful four-cylinder diesel in the range. Powered by the OM654 2.0-litre inline-four turbodiesel, it delivered 245 hp and 500 Nm of torque - later upgraded to 265 hp with the EQ Boost mild-hybrid system in 2021.

milestones.description: **2018** - W213 E 300d launched with OM654.920 engine, 180 kW (245 hp), 500 Nm, rear-wheel drive
**2018-2021** - E 300d available in saloon (W213), estate (S213), and cabriolet (A238) body styles
**2021** - Facelift introduces OM654.930 with EQ Boost mild-hybrid, 195 kW (265 hp), 550 Nm
**2021-2023** - E 300d 4MATIC available with 195 kW (265 hp) and 550 Nm
**2023** - W214 generation launched; E 300d badge replaced by E 300de plug-in hybrid diesel in some markets

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 300d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM654 engine that powers the E Class 300d is a modern, efficient diesel that replaced the OM651. While generally robust, timing chain wear and AdBlue system failures are the two most significant concerns. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the OM654 in the E Class 300d Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: The OM654 uses a timing chain mounted at the rear of the engine. Individual bolts or chain links can wear under specific driving conditions. A recall was issued for certain E-Class (213 platform) vehicles with the OM654 engine due to this issue. Extended oil change intervals and stop-start operation accelerate wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain tensioner replacement and wear measurement
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles; effective if rattle is minimal

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets - engine-out job on OM654
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has stretched or rattle persists

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 with new timing components and upgraded parts
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has failed causing valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W213 E Class 300d is worth £18,000-£30,000 depending on condition and mileage【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. Given the high residual value of the 300d, a rebuilt engine with warranty is almost always justifiable if the rest of the car is sound. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: The OM654 timing chain recall indicates this is a known issue - if your E Class 300d is within the affected range, check if the recall work has been completed. The cold-start rattle is your early warning - don't ignore it. A specialist timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,200 is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement if the chain fails. Given the £18,000+ value of most W213 E 300d examples, preventative chain work is a wise investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM654 Mercedes E Class 300d engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System Failure - The E Class 300d Emissions Weakness
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue system (Selective Catalytic Reduction) uses a pump integrated into the AdBlue tank. The pump can fail, or the AdBlue injector can become clogged. Tank crystallisation and NOx sensor failure are also common.

repairOptions.longevity: 40,000-60,000 miles; effective if injector is clogged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of complete AdBlue tank assembly with integrated pump
repairOptions.longevity: When pump has failed or tank has crystallised

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 with all emissions components
repairOptions.longevity: Not typically required for AdBlue issues alone

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W213 £18,000-£30,000). On a car worth this much, repairing the AdBlue system is always the right call - don't risk the £800+ repair escalating by ignoring warning lights.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue system issues are frustrating but rarely require engine replacement. The most cost-effective approach is early diagnosis - if you see an AdBlue warning light, get it checked promptly. The £250-£450 injector replacement is far cheaper than a £800-£1,400 tank replacement if crystallisation has occurred. Use genuine AdBlue fluid and avoid letting the tank run dry to prevent pump damage.
problems.cta: -> Get OM654 Mercedes E Class 300d AdBlue system quotes

problems.h4: Camshaft & Rocker Wear - The OM654 Top-End Issue
problems.rootCause: Camshaft and rocker arm wear has been reported on OM654 engines, particularly around 100,000 miles. This can cause noise, reduced performance, and eventually valvetrain failure if not addressed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of camshafts, rocker arms and followers
Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 with new valvetrain components
repairOptions.longevity: When wear has caused catastrophic engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W213 £18,000-£30,000). At this vehicle value, £900-£1,600 for camshaft work is a relatively minor expense to protect a high-value asset.
problems.recommendation: Camshaft and rocker wear is a known issue on higher-mileage OM654 engines. Regular oil changes (8,000-10,000 miles) with the correct specification oil are critical to prevent premature wear. If you hear unusual top-end noise from your E Class 300d, have it inspected promptly - early intervention can prevent a £3,200+ engine replacement.
